Sergio / team / Anna — attached is a concise comparison and the evaluation acceptance criteria you asked for. Summary below:

Short comparison (operational highlights):
- Hosted API: fastest time-to-value, lower upfront cost, limited for PHI unless we set a Dedicated tenancy or contract-level BAA (not typical). Good for non-PHI analytics and pilot traffic.
- Dedicated: customer-dedicated GPU pool, can be put in a customer VPC for stronger isolation; recommended if you need predictable throughput and lower nominal latency; supports our SLA and reserved pricing.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full control, required for PHI if your policy forbids third-party managed hosted environments. Highest ops/engineering lift and cost.

Technical recommendation for Greenleaf (short):
- For production PHI flows: Dedicated with VPC peering in us-east (primary).
- For non-PHI analytics: use Hosted in us-west as cheaper overflow.
- Plan for a hybrid cutover: pilot 2 weeks on Hosted (non-PHI), 2-week Dedicated pilot for PHI lanes, rollback window of 48 hours.

Evaluation acceptance criteria (proposed):
- Latency SLO: p95 < 120 ms for EHR lookup (us-east) under 200 concurrent requests.
- Throughput: sustained 300 qps for batch scoring jobs in analytics lane.
- Security: SOC2 Type II evidence provided; network diagram and BAA template delivered.
- Quality/regression: generation/regression tests on the provided prompt set with no >5% drop in key intent accuracy vs baseline.
- Observability: token-level cost and latency traces available and accessible to Greenleaf during the trial.

Proposed timeline (condensed):
- 2027-03-15: delivery of SOC2 + network diagram + acceptance criteria doc (we can bundle into a single packet).
- 2027-03-16 to 2027-03-29: evaluation window (pilot split Hosted non-PHI + Dedicated PHI lanes).
- 2027-03-30: decision checkpoint and contract signature target 2027-03-31 if green.

Attachments: eval_criteria.csv (small), sample_network_diagram.png

I can tighten the p95 targets if Greenleaf supplies a realistic traffic trace.

—Karthik
